Accessing and versioning UCDP data

Source: vignettes/accessing-and-versioning.Rmd
accessing-and-versioning.Rmd

This vignette explains how ucdpR separates discovery, selection, download, and import. The examples first use a small synthetic catalog so that the vignette can be rebuilt without network access.

library(ucdpR)

catalog <- tibble::tibble(
  dataset = c(
    "UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED)",
    "UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED)",
    "UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset"
  ),
  version = c("25.1", "24.1", "25.1"),
  variant = NA_character_,
  section = c(
    "Disaggregated Event Datasets",
    "Disaggregated Event Datasets",
    "Yearly Datasets"
  ),
  format = "csv",
  url = c(
    "https://example.org/ged-251.csv",
    "https://example.org/ged-241.csv",
    "https://example.org/prio-251.csv"
  ),
  file_name = c("ged-251.csv", "ged-241.csv", "prio-251.csv"),
  source = c("current", "historical", "current")
)

Discover and search

ucdp_catalog() reads UCDP’s official download pages rather than relying on a hard-coded package inventory. A regular-expression search can then narrow the catalog by dataset, variant, version, or section.

ucdp_search("Georeferenced|GED", catalog)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   dataset                  version variant section format url   file_name source
#>   <chr>                    <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>     <chr> 
#> 1 UCDP Georeferenced Even… 25.1    NA      Disagg… csv    http… ged-251.… curre…
#> 2 UCDP Georeferenced Even… 24.1    NA      Disagg… csv    http… ged-241.… histo…
ucdp_search("Yearly", catalog)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   dataset                  version variant section format url   file_name source
#>   <chr>                    <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>     <chr> 
#> 1 UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflic… 25.1    NA      Yearly… csv    http… prio-251… curre…

The equivalent live workflow is:

current <- ucdp_catalog()
all_releases <- ucdp_catalog(include_historical = TRUE)
ucdp_search("Battle[- ]Related Deaths", current)

Inspect and pin releases

ucdp_versions() sorts matching releases from newer to older. Supplying an exact version to a download or import call prevents a later UCDP update from silently changing an analysis.

ucdp_versions("ged", format = "csv", catalog = catalog)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   dataset                  version variant section format url   file_name source
#>   <chr>                    <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>     <chr> 
#> 1 UCDP Georeferenced Even… 25.1    NA      Disagg… csv    http… ged-251.… curre…
#> 2 UCDP Georeferenced Even… 24.1    NA      Disagg… csv    http… ged-241.… histo…
ucdp_update_available("ged", version = "24.1", catalog = catalog)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   dataset installed_version current_version update_available
#>   <chr>   <chr>             <chr>           <lgl>           
#> 1 ged     24.1              25.1            TRUE
ucdp_update_available("ged", version = "25.1", catalog = catalog)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   dataset installed_version current_version update_available
#>   <chr>   <chr>             <chr>           <lgl>           
#> 1 ged     25.1              25.1            FALSE
ged_path <- ucdp_download(
  "ged", version = "25.1", format = "csv", dest_dir = "data-raw"
)

ged <- ucdp_get("ged", version = "25.1", format = "csv")
attr(ged_path, "md5")
attr(ged, "ucdp_source")

Use ucdp_download() when the original file should remain in the project. Use ucdp_get() when the immediate goal is an imported R object. Historical monthly Candidate releases can be pinned in the same way, for example with version = "25.0.12".

Resolve variants explicitly

Some datasets contain several downloadable variants. Search first, then make the intended level visible in the analysis script.

ucdp_search("Battle[- ]Related Deaths")
brd_dyadic <- ucdp_get("brd", variant = "dyadic", format = "csv")

Record citation guidance

The data version and UCDP’s requested dataset citation should both be recorded.

ucdp_cite("ged")
ucdp_codebook("ged", version = "25.1", dest_dir = "documentation")

Catalog discovery is dynamic, but analytical inputs should be static. A useful project therefore combines live discovery with an exact version, a retained file or checksum, and the corresponding documentation.
